A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InertialAR. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original unconditional molecule-generation experiments on QM9, GEOM-Drugs, and B3LYP, plus class-conditional generation and editing results.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation results and adds canonical-frame robustness analyses and component ablations in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The canonicalization, axis-wise rotary encoding, Nyström features, hierarchical type/coordinate prediction, losses, and guidance procedure remain substantively unchanged. GeoRoPE becomes GeoPE, RoPE-3D becomes ManhattanPE, and Nyström encoding becomes EuclideanPE, with equivalent computational formulas. The ablated alternatives do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: QM9, GEOM-Drugs, B3LYP-1M, and the five class-conditional targets are retained. Appendix E.1 adds Gaussian-perturbed coordinate scenarios on QM9 and Drugs, extending coverage to noisy inputs without introducing another molecular domain.

E2.justification: EDM-Bridge gains an actual results row in Table 1; v1 named it in the baseline discussion but reported no corresponding results. E-NFs matches v1's EFN/ENF naming, while the B3LYP and class-conditional comparator sets remain EDM and Geo2Seq.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends evaluation design with Gaussian perturbations from 10^-4 to 10^-7 angstroms, full-dataset degeneracy scans, and controlled loss and atom-ordering ablations. Table 1 explicitly identifies MiDi re-evaluation under the EDM protocol. Existing dataset splits remain unchanged; Appendix E acknowledges a different ablation configuration from the headline experiments without specifying its parameters.

E4.justification: New Appendix E tests anchor stability under coordinate perturbations, principal-moment degeneracy, diffusion loss versus direct L2 regression, and canonical versus raw atom ordering. v1 asserted that direct regression performed poorly but supplied none of these quantitative analyses. The existing CFG editing examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new robustness frequencies and ablation tables provide point results without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise multiple results: InertialAR's QM9 validity changes from 97.4% to 97.3%, Drugs validity from 96.8% to 98.0%, and B3LYP molecule stability from 24.2% to 24.7%. MiDi's results are replaced under its explicitly revised evaluation protocol. Tables 4–7 add robustness and ablation findings, including L2 validity of 24.7% versus 97.4% for diffusion loss. Table 3 is unchanged; these revisions do not establish uniform same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 now states distinct-principal-moment and deterministic-anchor assumptions. Appendix D reconciles v1's conflicting anchor conditions and revises the proof using separate initial and final anchor coordinates, replacing its erroneous rigidity explanation. Appendix C corrects the Nyström block-matrix expression. The formal positional-encoding and complex/quaternion derivations in v1 Appendices E–F are removed.

C1.justification: The abstract increases claimed unconditional benchmark leadership from 7/10 to 8/10 metrics, consistent with the revised Table 1 comparison. The introduction explicitly claims the first generation-ready use of inertial-frame canonicalization for autoregressive 3D generation. The central method and class-conditional contribution claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 briefly treats degenerate frames as physically equivalent. v2 substantially develops the limitations of nonunique PCA frames and perturbation-induced axis flips, distinguishes practical robustness from theoretically perfect canonicalization, and discusses frame averaging as a possible extension. Appendix E interprets the new tests as supporting practical stability, while qualifying comparison between ablation and headline configurations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and clarifies ascending eigenvalue ordering and RDKit canonical-SMILES serialization. It first discloses exclusion of nine QM9 molecules and one Drugs molecule with degenerate principal moments from training. These disclosures do not establish when the implementation choices changed; detailed training configurations remain absent.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.2 positions the method relative to Frame Averaging and canonicalization-discontinuity research, citing Puny et al. and Dym et al.; Zhou et al. and Ni et al. add biological applications. Novelty is more explicitly located in autoregressive generation. References associated with the deleted positional-encoding tutorial are removed, while the main molecular-generation literature remains.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, contributions, canonicalization discussion, and conclusion, and changes encoding terminology throughout. The appendix narrative is substantially reorganized: related work gains a subsection, the positional-encoding and quaternion tutorials disappear, and empirical analyses replace them. An Impact Statement is added.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two columns. Table 1 gains a backbone column and protocol annotation, Table 3 uses class-grouped sections, and four analysis tables are added. Figure 1 is relabeled, Figure 2 changes from a horizontal strip to a grid, and the retained editing and class-mapping figures exchange numbering and placement. v1's complex-number Figure 8 is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the retained method by correcting inconsistencies in the frame-sign argument, stating its applicability conditions, and supplying previously missing component and robustness tests. The MiDi comparison also becomes more transparent. Important limitations remain: ablation configurations and uncertainty are insufficiently documented, and the broad robustness interpretation exceeds what tiny perturbations and an anchor-change proxy directly establish. These limits temper, but do not outweigh, the gains in mathematical clarity and empirical validation.
